title: Interpreting Powder Morphology of Uranium Ore Concentrates Using Machine Learning and Scanning Electron Microscopy for Nuclear Forensics Applications
content: Nuclear forensics is the examination of nuclear materials using analytical techniques to determine material provenance [1]. Morphological and textural characteristics of actinide powders can be linked to the conditions of formation, which can inform provenance assessments. Traditionally this is a laborious process that requires hours of manual segmentation combined with high dimensional statistical analyses and interpretation by subject matter experts (SME). As a result, assessments based on powder morphology are commonly confusing and difficult to communicate [2]. This leads to a necessity to produce a robust, high-fidelity numerical method which can be applied to images without the need of SME intervention.
